_meta.indication: JANUVIA is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus as monotherapy and in combination therapy with metformin or a PPARγ agonist (e.g., thiazolidinediones) when the single agent does not provide adequate glycemic control

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel treatment, 24 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus with HbA1c ≥7% and ≤10% while off any anti-diabetic therapy for at least 8 weeks
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in mean HbA1c from baseline at study endpoint
pivotal_trials.result: Sitagliptin monotherapy lowered HbA1c significantly vs placebo; in P021 the least square mean difference from placebo was -0.79 for the 100 mg dose and -0.94 for the 200 mg dose

pivotal_trials.design: 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in patients on a stable dose of metformin (at least 1500 mg daily) with HbA1c 7 to 10%
pivotal_trials.population: Type 2 diabetics on stable metformin (at least 1500 mg daily) with HbA1c between 7 and 10%
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in mean HbA1c from baseline at study endpoint
pivotal_trials.n: 701 randomized (464 sitagliptin 100 mg, 237 placebo); 677 (96.6%) in MITT analysis
pivotal_trials.result: Sitagliptin 100 mg added to metformin gave greater HbA1c reduction than placebo; LSM difference from placebo -0.65 (p<0.001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and more common than placebo) were upper respiratory tract infection, nasopharyngitis, and headache; in monotherapy nasopharyngitis occurred in 23 (5.2%) vs 12 (3.3%) placebo. Overall hypoglycemia incidence with JANUVIA 100 mg was similar to placebo (1.2% vs 0.9%)
target_moa: Sitagliptin is an inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase IV (DPP-IV), the enzyme responsible for metabolism of the incretin hormones GLP-1 and GIP; inhibiting DPP-IV prolongs the half-life of endogenous incretins, enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion and reducing glucagon release

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was scheduled or held; the mechanism of action had already been a target of therapy (exenatide) and the drug presented no efficacy or safety issues requiring advisory committee deliberation

description.text: Added combination therapy with a sulfonylurea (alone or with metformin) and a non-inferiority study vs glipizide added on to metformin

citations.quote: S-002: Additions to the Package Insert (PI) describing the results of (1) a study of combination therapy with a sulfonylurea when the single agent alone does not provide adequate glycemic control and in combination therapy with a sulfonylurea plus metformin when dual therapy does not provide adequate glycemic control, and (2) a non-inferiority study comparing Januvia to glipizide in patients without adequate glycemic control on metformin.

description.text: Added use of sitagliptin in combination with metformin and a PPARγ agonist as adjunct to diet and exercise in adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin plus PPARγ agonist

citations.quote: The "Prior Approval" supplemental applications S-010, S-011 and S-012 provide for the use of Januvia (sitagliptin) in combination with metformin and a PPAR\gamma agonist as an adjunct to diet and exercise in adult patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus who are inadequately controlled on combination therapy with metformin and a PPAR\gamma agonist (S-010), for the use of Januvia (sitagliptin) as combination therapy with a PPAR\gamma agonist (S-011), and for the use of Januvia in combination with insulin, alone or in combination with metformin (S-012). The "Prior Approval" supplement S-014 contains proposed safety related labeling changes to the Package Insert regarding the risk of pancreatitis as well as a newly created Medication Guide, and a proposed Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). The Package Insert containing the pancreatitis-related changes was approved under supplemental application S-013 on December 28, 2009.

description.text: Added pancreatitis incidence from controlled clinical trials to the Clinical Trials Experience section of the label

citations.quote: These "Prior Approval" supplemental new drug applications propose to include information regarding the incidence of pancreatitis associated with the use of sitagliptin in controlled clinical trials in the Clinical Trials Experience section of the package insert for Januvia (S-015), and the addition of "constipation, headache, vomiting" in the Postmarketing Experience section of the package insert, and corresponding patient-friendly text in the Medication Guide for Januvia (S-018).

description.text: Added efficacy/safety data from Study P845 on continuation of sitagliptin during initiation and titration of insulin glargine in type 2 diabetes to the prescribing information

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications provide for the addition of information from Study P845 titled, "A Phase III, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial to Study the Efficacy and Safety of the Continuation of Sitagliptin Compared with the Withdrawal of Sitagliptin During Initiation and Titration of Insulin Glargine (LANTUS) in Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus," in the prescribing information.

description.text: Added use in pediatric patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus based on Protocol 083 for sitagliptin (Januvia)

citations.quote: Changes to the Prescribing Information and Medication Guide based on the results of Protocol 083, entitled "A Phase III, Multicenter, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Sitagliptin in Pediatric Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Inadequate Glycemic Control."

summary.text: First-cycle standard approval of a first-in-class DPP-4 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes, based on reductions in HbA1c, a well-accepted surrogate for improved outcomes in diabetes; no advisory committee was convened and pediatric studies were deferred/waived under PREA

citations.quote: This is the first cycle review for this first in class agent.
Like most recent therapies for DM, this drug will be approved on the basis of a very well accepted and characterized surrogate for improved outcomes – the HgbA1c.
We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for ages birth to 10 years, inclusive, and deferring pediatric studies for ages 11 to 16 years, inclusive, for this application.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of type 2 diabetes in pediatric patients ages 11 to 16, inclusive
